_comment: Which delivered frame folders become which den find. Run with:
Everything under assets/main_menu/environment/animated/ is OUTPUT, not source.
The delivery in src_root is never modified. Same arrangement as the fox --
see tools/fox_clips.json and the header of tools/den_import.py.
src_root is where the artist's delivery was unpacked: the only machine-specific
'scale' is 0.5 for everything here. The art arrived about twice den size, and a
half reduction is the one that maps four source pixels onto one without dropping
rows unevenly. Do not put an arbitrary scale here -- den_import.py refuses
anything that isn't 1.0 or a clean 1/2, 1/3, 1/4. See its header.
'fps' is the playback rate den.gd gives the find. Nothing is measured from the
source, so these are a first guess: fire wants to be brisk, leaves want to drift.
'skins' groups several folders under one find, for the fireplace. Each entry
becomes its own frame folder; the find shows one at a time and the player
right-clicks to cycle. A find with 'src' instead of 'skins' is a plain one.

finds._note: Ten designs of one object, so one find with ten appearances rather than ten drawer slots. Order is the artist's numbering; skin 0 is what a new den gets.

skins.name: modern
skins._note: V1 and V2 were both delivered. V2 is the later pass.

skins.name: stove
skins._note: Much taller than the rest (a flue) and comes with its own log baskets.

finds._note: Hangs rather than stands -- the first animated wall find. Imported at full size, unlike everything else here: it was delivered much smaller than the fireplaces (87x101 against ~320x250), so the half that right-sized them left this reading as a sprig. At 1.0 it lands at 87x101 -- still small next to a 150px bookshelf, which is what a hanging plant should be -- and the pixels are the artist's own, untouched.
